title: Multi Agent AI and Network Knowledge Graphs for Change — Ola Mabadeje, Cisco
talk_summary: Cisco's Outshift built a change-management system with a natural-language interface, a planner plus specialized ReAct agents, and a layered network knowledge graph/digital twin for impact assessment and test execution. They fine-tuned the graph-query agent with schema/examples to cut token use and latency, and emphasize extrinsic evaluation tied to customer outcomes.

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune structured-query agent with schema and examples
takeaways.what_they_do: They initially used RAG to query the knowledge graph, but it burned tokens and time; they fine-tuned a query agent with schema information and example queries instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we did some finetuning of of the of of this agent with some schema information as well as example queries

takeaways.technique: Layered knowledge schema with query routing
takeaways.what_they_do: They layer the network graph so an agent can go directly to the relevant layer, such as raw config for drift checks or multiple layers for reachability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to go to all of the layers of the graph you just go straight down to the raw configuration file

takeaways.what_they_do: They combine a knowledge-graph snapshot with executable network tools to run generated tests against a digital twin and attach results to the ticket.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a digital twin again is a cons combination of the knowledge graph, a set of tools that you can use to run the test

takeaways.technique: Mandatory impact assessment and test plan artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Planner/assistant agents summarize the ticket, create an impact assessment, and generate test cases with expected results before approval and execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: come up with a list of tests that you have to run to be able to make sure that this firewall rule change doesn't make a big impact

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents on the Cisco side and agents on the ITSM side exchange work by attaching summaries, assessments, test plans, and reports to the ticket.
takeaways.evidence_quote: two separate systems but agents talking to each other

takeaways.technique: Extrinsic outcome metrics tied to use case
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate the knowledge graph, agents, and digital twin with quantifiable extrinsic metrics mapped back to the customer's use case rather than intrinsic model metrics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're looking at extrinsic metrics particularly not intrinsic ones because we want to map this back to the customer's use case
